annotations.annotation_text: ALP invocation "Livvy" on page 553 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): Anna Livia Plurabelle, the mother-river personifying the Liffey, surfaces here amid the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. In this Age of Men passage, her feminine current of forgiveness and renewal flows through the dream landscape, carrying Dublin's history from source to sea.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Hart, Clive. Structure and Motif in Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/structuremotifin0000hart
Mink, Louis O. A Finnegans Wake Gazetteer. https://archive.org/details/finneganswakegaz0000mink
FWEET: ALP / River Liffey concordance. https://www.fweet.org

annotations.annotation_text: Fall/resurrection motif "wall" on page 553 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): Tim Finnegan tumbling from his ladder, Humpty Dumpty shattering from the wall, Adam falling in Eden — all converge within the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. The comic-cosmic Fall during the Age of Men phase demands its counterpart: resurrection through the whiskey-splash of the water of life (uisce beatha).
sources: The Ballad of Tim Finnegan's Wake. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegan%27s_Wake
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Opie, Iona and Peter. The Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes. https://archive.org/details/oxforddictionary0000unse_m4u1
